response.description:
Resource health metrics in connection monitor brings resource health and key performance metrics into the Connection
Monitor test topology, powered by Network Watcher topology. Until now, the
topology showed the path between source and destination, but it didn't show the
health of the resources along that path. When a test reported packet loss or
high latency, customers had to switch between tabs and blades to check each
resource's health and metrics. That slowed down investigations and made it hard
to connect the dots. With this release, health and metrics now appear directly
in the topology. Customers can now click any resource in the connection monitor topology to see its resource health status and time-series metrics in
the same view. For example, selecting a load balancer shows its health along
with data path availability, health probe status, SNAT connection count and SYN count. Customers can view these metrics alongside connection monitor's own
packet loss and latency over the same time window. This makes it easy to see
whether a drop in a resource's health lines up with a connectivity issue. This enhancement brings loss, latency, health and
topology together in one view. When a resource is unhealthy, its metrics are a
click away, with no need to switch tabs or tools. Customers can correlate
resource health signals with connectivity results to reach the root cause
faster. It requires no setup and is available for all new and existing connection monitor tests. By surfacing resource health directly in the connection monitor topology, Azure helps customers go from detecting a
connectivity issue to understanding its cause faster, so they can resolve
problems sooner and keep their workloads running reliably. Learn more.
response.title: Public Preview: Azure Network Watcher – Resource health and topology in connection monitor tests
